{"self_assessment": "Impact: I laid the belly line (stroke 2) of our left-facing fish, which is about half of the body outline. It joined the top line at the tail crossing, and the pre-push check showed all 97 standing dominoes connected to the start, both fin tips included. I can't say whether the judge recognized the fish, because I only saw the table before the push. Our plan was Hana's, and I executed my part of it rather than shaping it.

Execution: The belly went in cleanly with no breaks, and I reported when it reached the tail. I checked the joints and the crossing and found only a few harmless pale strays beside the crossing. I left them alone rather than risk a bump, but I never confirmed they couldn't interfere. After the build I stayed hands-off to avoid bumps. One slip: when I finished early I jumped onto the lower fin without checking that Jack was already on it. He was about two thirds done, and Hana then judged the fin was bending off the upper one and relaid it. That created some overlap and could have caused a collision, and I should have looked or asked first.

Collaboration: I kept the table updated on progress, and when Jack and Hana asked me to stay off the fin I did so straight away. I confirmed my checks matched Hana's so we all had the same picture. My early offer to cover the fin was well meant but badly timed.

Leadership: Hana led the plan and I took my assigned stroke and stayed in my lane. I did not take a leadership role. My contribution was reliable status updates, giving the manager clear answers at each check-in, and helping the table keep to a hands-off discipline near the deadline. Next time I would confirm who is working on a stroke before offering to take it over."}
